title: nepotest test file
description: Unit tests for a NEPO program of the Edison V2 (see docs/ai/nepo-unit-testing.md). nepotest.validate_spec checks the same rules plus names against the program.

program.description: path of the NEPO export XML, relative to this file

bundle.description: path of the cached conversion (EdPy + source map), relative to this file

block_id.description: the id of the test block, if the test was built with NEPO test blocks

call.description: a NEPO function name: call it instead of running the whole program

globals.description: global variables to set before the call (a test of a simulation world: from the start, its set-up)

should.description: fail: the test passes if its expectations (or the checks of its simulation, not the rules of its world) fail, and fails if they hold; default pass

skip.description: true: the test doesn't run (outcome skipped)

simulation.description: A test of a simulation world: the robot starts at one of the world's starts in a drawn world on the Lab's own simulator (its backgrounds and wall, obstacles, coloured areas, robot, sensors), the whole program runs (until it ends, until the robot touches the 'until' area, or for max_time_ms), and the checks decide: the test passes only if every check holds and the program doesn't fail. It runs in the Tests tab (the command line skips it). Its world events may only be clap and key. Units: cm from the background's top left corner; x right, y down; angles in degrees, counterclockwise as seen from above.

world_block_id.description: the id of the world's block, if the test was built with NEPO test blocks

background.description: peach: the tests' own plain floor (#f7d1b3, 300 x 200 cm, no wall); the others are the Lab's simulator's

starts.description: where the robot can start (the pose of the wheel axle's centre)

until.description: the id of an area (goal, fail or coloured): the run ends when the robot touches it (if it starts on it: when it touches it again)

simCheck.description: a check of a test of a simulation world. reaches: the robot touches the item (an area; none: any goal area) at some time; never_touches: never (none: any fail area); ends_in: the whole robot is in the item (an area) at the end; never_bumps: the robot never bumps into the item (an obstacle; none: anything, the wall too). The robot's behaviour, measured in every frame of the simulator: does: from after_ms on, the robot always does it; whenever: whenever the condition (what the robot's sensors see) has held for after_ms, the robot does it, for as long as it holds (never held: nothing is checked); after: after each event (claps and key presses: of the set-up), the robot does it at some moment within within_ms (no event: nothing is checked); variable: the global variable at the end. rule: it came from a world's rules (until 2026-10-30); it counts like any other check

does.description: what the robot does (does, whenever, after): driving and turning from its position and heading (forward: at least 1 cm/s along its heading; turning: at least 10 degrees/s), its LEDs, its sound

after_ms.description: does: from when on (default 100); whenever: how long the condition must have held, the time to react (default 0: the program reacts in the frame after it sensed something)

percent.description: the light conditions: below / above this %

variable.description: a global variable of the program

simItem.description: a line to follow (drawn like the background's track: a black core on a white band), or one of the simulator's objects: a rect (top left x, y; w, h), a circle (centre x, y; r) or a triangle (points), as an obstacle, a coloured area the sensors see (color), a goal area or a fail area

name.description: what the blocks show (no name: its kind and number, e.g. 'Goal 2')

smooth.description: a curve through the points instead of straight segments

width.description: the black core in cm (default 1.48, as the background's track)

matcher.description: keys of an action (action, dir, block, block_id, function, port, mode, direction, power, distance_cm, degrees, power_left, power_right, frequency_hz, duration_ms, ms, value, file, sensor, t, t_end) or of a call (function, args, returns)

actions.description: found in this order, other actions may be in between

oneOf.description: number of actions matching each matcher

calls.description: NEPO function calls, in this order, others may be in between

error.description: null (default): no runtime error; 'any'; a kind such as 'division_by_zero'; or a matcher on kind, block_id, block_type, function

covers.description: block ids that must be executed

states.description: what the robot is doing, and when (nepotest/states.py)

distance_cm.description: at the end: the distance driven, mean of both wheels, backward negative

heading_deg.description: at the end: the change of heading, counterclockwise (left) positive

end_position.description: at the end: where the robot is relative to its start (ahead = its first heading, left of it), within tol_cm

power.description: a number: rounded like the robot does (45 to 54 mean 50); a matcher: the power it runs at
only for forward, backward and the turns

frequency_hz.description: only for tone: the NEPO frequency

window.description: ms of program time; left out: from the program's start (after the setup block) / to the end of the run

edge.description: obstacle: when it appears (default) or disappears

color.description: line: when the line tracker starts to see this color

for_ms.description: the time the state held, in total

stateExpectation.description: exactly one timing; within_ms and each go with after, delay_ms with while
